subject: Demo follow-up: implementation notes and rate-limit strategy
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Demo follow-up: implementation notes and rate-limit strategy

Hi Alyssa — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the implementation plan with your SRE and infra constraints.

Recap:
- You want Redwood for semantic search + a lightweight re-ranker in front of results; embeddings for candidate retrieval and a small on-the-fly re-ranker to improve precision.
- Expected steady-state: 2–3 qps; burst to ~20 qps for hourly report runs.
- Sensitive data: PII-filtered; you prefer API key + IP allowlist and would consider VPC/private for Prod.

Primary questions for engineering:
1) Auth: will you be able to use API keys with IP allowlist, or do you need mTLS/KMS-managed keys?
2) Routing: do you want dedicated capacity for production SLA or is hosted shared OK for PoC?
3) Structured outputs/tool-calling: re-ranker will call an internal enrichment service after scoring — does that need guaranteed once-only semantics?
4) Rate limits & retries: what's the acceptable client retry behavior (e.g., exponential backoff, max retries)?

What we propose for PoC (high level):
- SDK integration: use Redwood SDK (JS/python) with built-in retry middleware and automatic request-id insertion.
- Auth: API key + IP allowlist for PoC; Private deployment or Dedicated pool for Prod if you need compliance SLA.
- Routing: route embeddings-heavy calls to a dedicated GPU pool; small re-ranker calls to lower-cost CPU-backed fast path.
- Quotas: tenant-level token quota + per-endpoint QPS. Token-bucket with burst capacity configured to match your hourly burst profile.
- Idempotency: recommend client-supplied Idempotency-Key (X-Idempotency-Key) for any operation that creates persistent state; for pure inference calls we advise dedup by request-id for safe retries of 429/5xx.
- 429 handling: exponential backoff with jitter (client-side) and server-side 429 response should include Retry-After and request-id.

Attached: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft timeline + milestones).

Next steps: can you send a short CSV of expected query size distribution and confirm auth preference? I’ll loop eng to propose an exact retry/quota config.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive 
Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finlytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: implementation notes and rate-limit strategy

Thanks Dylan — nice recap. Quick answers and additional context from our side: we attached a small CSV with expected per-hour bins.

Answers:
- Auth: API keys with IP allowlist for now. We prefer not to do mTLS for the PoC; may require KM S integration for Prod.
- Routing: PoC can run on hosted shared; Prod should be Dedicated for predictable latency (we have internal SLAs).
- Structured output/tool-calling: the re-ranker will trigger a downstream enrichment call that writes metadata back to our DB — need near-duplicate suppression. Ideally, enrichment calls are idempotent or accept an idempotency key.
- Rate limits: we can tolerate up to 5s tail latency for rerank calls; retry budget is limited since our enrichment pipeline has side effects. For inference-only endpoints (embeddings/search), automatic retries are OK.

Workload notes (from CSV): steady 2.5 qps, hourly spike ~18 qps for 3–4 minutes, bulk backfills that run overnight (burst up to 120 qps for 10–15 minutes). Embedding vector size target: 1536 dims.

Can you please confirm recommended client headers (names) for idempotency and request-tracking, and whether Redwood provides a server-side dedupe option?

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Data Platforms
FinLytics

---
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Demo follow-up: implementation notes and rate-limit strategy

Forwarding Alyssa's responses — FinLytics confirmed PoC auth (API key + IP allowlist), steady 2–3 qps with short bursts up to 18 qps, and overnight bulk bursts up to 120 qps for a few minutes. They want idempotency for enrichment calls that write to their DB; inference-only calls can be retried.

Alyssa asked: "Can you please confirm recommended client headers (names) for idempotency and request-tracking, and whether Redwood provides a server-side dedupe option?"

Quick ask for Priyom/Connor: please draft a short recommended config we can send to FinLytics that covers:
- SDK usage pattern: where to plug retry middleware and how to generate request ids/keys.
- Auth & routing recommendation for PoC vs Prod (what to enable now to make Prod switch painless).
- Concrete quota settings to support their bursts (token-bucket params: steady-rate, burst-capacity, refill interval), and how to escalate to Dedicated pool if bursts exceed limits.
- 429/Retry guidance for their two classes of calls:
  * Inference-only (embeddings, search): automatic client retry on 429/5xx; exponential backoff with full jitter, initial delay 200–500ms, cap 8 retries; include X-Request-ID.
  * Side-effecting enrichment calls: require Idempotency-Key (X-Idempotency-Key). Server will dedupe if key seen within 24h window and return 200/duplicate with original request-id. For non-idempotent calls we should NOT auto-retry beyond 1 attempt.

I attached a quick infra diagram (redwood_infra_arch.png) and a link to our rate_limit_and_retries playbook; feel free to paste any code snippet. We'll need this to be customer-facing by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Dylan

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo follow-up: implementation notes and rate-limit strategy

Adding the recommended configuration for the note to FinLytics. Paste this back to the thread when you send.

RECOMMENDED CUSTOMER-FACING CONFIG (PoC -> Prod):
- SDK: use the official Redwood SDK (js/python). Enable "retry-middleware" and "request-tracking" modules. Middleware auto-inserts X-Request-ID when missing; app should set X-Idempotency-Key for any enrichment/write operations.

- Idempotency headers:
  * X-Idempotency-Key: client-generated UUIDv4 for any call that mutates downstream systems; server stores key for 24 hours and returns duplicate marker + original request-id.
  * X-Request-ID: optional per-request tracing id; Redwood will echo in responses (useful for logs).

- Retry policy suggestions:
  * Inference-only endpoints: retry on 429, 502, 503, 504. Backoff: initial=300ms, multiplier=2, max_delay=10s, full jitter. Max attempts=6 (so 5 retries).
  * Side-effecting enrichment (writes): DO NOT retry automatically. If client receives 429 for enrichment, surface to user and require explicit retry with same X-Idempotency-Key if safe.

- Quota & burst config (token-bucket):
  * steady_rate: 3 qps
  * burst_capacity: 60 tokens
  * refill_interval: 1s
  * night/backfill: request temporary quota bump via console or API; for PoC enable a soft-burst window to allow their 120 qps jobs for <= 15 minutes.

- Routing:
  * PoC: hosted shared with IP-allowlist + API key.
  * Prod: move embeddings to Dedicated GPU pool (pinned model/quantization), re-ranker to Dedicated CPU or low-latency host. Implement routing policy based on API key tags.

- Server-side dedupe: Redwood supports dedupe for requests with X-Idempotency-Key for 24h window. For long-running jobs we recommend storing the server-request-id returned in a system of record.

IMPLEMENTATION SNIPPET (JS pseudocode):
  // client: ensure idempotency for writes
  const idempotencyKey = uuid.v4();
  const res = await redwood.request('/enrich', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'X-Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey },
    body: payload
  });

  // client: retry middleware configured centrally for inference calls

MONITORING / ALERTS:
- Track 429 rate per-API key, 5xx rate, and tail-latency p95/p99.
- Create an alert when 429 rate > 5% sustained for 5 minutes.

NEXT STEPS:
1) Dylan: send this note + mutual_action_plan.xlsx + expected_workloads.csv to Alyssa.
2) FinLytics: confirm whether they want a temporary quota bump for overnight backfills or prefer to throttle.
3) Connor/Priyom: prepare a short snippet for the SDK readme and a configuration block for the Console (quota + routing).

I'll be on standby to iterate.

— Priyom
Senior Staff Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference
